messages:
jia (ml): Heads-up — nightly bring-up of mixlang-13b (int8-dyn, kv-cache off) shows a ~6 BLEU drop on JP-KO testset compared to fp16. curious if this is tokenization or quantization.

sam (research): Oof. Numbers?

jia (ml): baseline fp16 BLEU=28.3, int8-dyn BLEU=22.1. chrF dropped 0.6. COMET down from 0.42 -> 0.29.

marco (infra): build-bot shows the job config: `model: redwood/mixlang-13b:quant-int8-dyn`, `kv_cache: disabled`, `tokenizer: new-subword-v2`. CI artifact: https://ci.redwood/snapshots/184312

eva (linguist): Short sanity check: is the tokenizer handling Hangul+Kanji adjacency? Mixed script segmentation can glue characters into weird subtokens.

jia (ml): good point. Sample failure:

```
Input: 日本어로 번역해 주세요. 저는 한국 사람입니다.
FP16 output: "일본어로 번역해주세요. 저는 한국 사람입니다."
INT8 output: "日本어로 번역해주세요. 저는 한국 사람입니다."
```

jia (ml): Notice the first token switching to Japanese kanji in the int8 output — model seems to copy source script incorrectly. Might be tokenization mapping mismatch where kanji+hangul boundary tokens became OOV or mapped differently after tokenizer change.

sam (research): Could also be embedding table aliasing from quantization — similar hash collisions when using dynamic quant. Any log about tokenizer vocab size or merges?

jia (ml): tokenizer vocab size 52000, merges updated last week (new-subword-v2). I reran tokenization for the sample:

```
new-subword-v2.tokenize("日本어로 번역해 주세요.") -> ["日本", "어로", "로", " 번", "역", "해", " 주세요", "."]
old-subword.tokenize("日本어로 번역해 주세요.") -> ["日本어", "로", " 번", "역", "해", " 주세요", "."]
```

jia (ml): So segmentation changed — splits "日本" and "어" separately now. That could shift positional/segment embeddings and lead model to prefer copying kanji tokens.

eva (linguist): That segmentation looks like it separates a kanji cluster from following hangul syllable, which is risky. We should prefer keeping script-adjacent grapheme clusters intact where possible for translation.

marco (infra): For quick triage, can we re-run the same int8 job but with `tokenizer: old-subword` (the fp16 one) and see if BLEU recovers? I can spin it up but need a clear command.

jia (ml): I'll patch the job: `--model redwood/mixlang-13b:quant-int8-dyn --tokenizer old-subword --kv_cache disabled --eval-set jp-ko-nightly` and kick it.

build-bot: Job queued: job/1843124601. ETA ~25m.

sam (research): Meanwhile, can we run quick per-token log-probs for that sample to see where distribution shifts? If the int8 model suddenly favors kanji token probability > hangul, that points to embedding/quant mismatch.

jia (ml): Ran local probe on a dev checkpoint (smaller). FP16 logprobs around token 1: [P("日本어")=0.62, P("日本")=0.03, P("日本어로")=0.18]; INT8: P("日本")=0.55, P("日本어")=0.06. So distribution moved to split token.

eva (linguist): That aligns with segmentation change. Two-pronged: tokenizer merges + model learned mixed tokens during training. Quantization likely exacerbates since int8 can distort small differences.

sam (research): Action items: (1) re-run int8 with old tokenizer, (2) rerun int8 with kv-cache enabled to rule out caching side-effects, (3) add a focused eval of script-boundary segmentation examples.

jia (ml): agreed. I'll add a small eval slice of 1k mixed-script sentences (JP-KO, JP-ZH, ZH-KO) — want chrF, BLEU, and a raw sample diff.

marco (infra): Job/1843124601 finished: int8+old-tokenizer BLEU=27.9 (chrF drop only 0.05 vs fp16). So tokenizer change is the main culprit.

jia (ml): Nice. That suggests revert tokenizer change for release. But we should also add a guard in onboarding: compare tokenization segmentation statistics vs baseline for mixed-script locales and fail if OOV/increase in splits > threshold.

eva (linguist): Also ping content teams — some downstream postprocessors assume script-preserving tokens.

sam (research): For model-side hardening, we should test int8 sensitivity: run quantization-aware retrain or per-channel quant instead of per-tensor to see if distributional shifts reduce. But immediate fix = tokenizer revert.

jia (ml): I'll open a short PR to revert tokenizer merge list and a checklist item for onboarding: add mixed-script segmentation diff, sample-level BLEU check for locale pairs.

marco (infra): tagging @eng-ml for followups. :thumbsup:

build-bot: PR created: https://git.redwood/repo/changes/PR-3842
